chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: Repertoire and time signatures of the early band
summary: They played slow tunes and waltzes like Careless Love and Over the Waves, mostly in common time rather than marches.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: In those days what kind of time signatures did you play in?

Well, we'd play slow tunes. Naturally, we all knew how to play slow tunes like "Careless Love" and "Over The Waves" was one of the tunes... "Over The Waves" sometimes we played in a waltz. I remember "When We Was Young," "At Three O'Clock In The Morning," "Let Me Call You Sweetheart," "Who's Sorry Now?", which was originally a waltz. "Let The Rest of The World Go By."
When you say these bands were Ragtime, the music they called it was Ragtime, you think of Ragtime as

Cut time is what you called common time. We usually played common time, in which you just play 4/4 time and then you split it. The 2/4 time naturally more or less was for marches, but we never played anything like that.
